title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Multi-Agent Distillation Frameworks
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate subliminal bias transmission in multi-agent distillation frameworks. By analyzing token-level entanglement patterns in teacher-generated data, we identify hidden signals that propagate unintended behavioral traits to student models. Our approach combines mechanistic interpretability with adversarial filtering to isolate and neutralize these signals during distillation. We validate the method by training student models on datasets generated by biased teacher agents and measuring bias amplification in downstream tasks.
gap: Existing multi-agent distillation frameworks (ref-004, ref-009) assume knowledge transfer occurs through explicit reasoning traces, overlooking potential subliminal bias transmission via hidden data patterns (ref-014, ref-017).
approach: We implement a three-stage process: (1) mechanistic analysis to identify neuron populations correlated with bias signals, (2) adversarial filtering to generate counterfactual data samples that neutralize these signals, and (3) constrained distillation that penalizes bias-related activation patterns in student models.
evaluation: We evaluate using three metrics: (1) bias amplification factor compared to baseline distillation, (2) task performance retention on factual/mathematical benchmarks, and (3) transferability of mitigation across different teacher-student architectures. Baselines include standard distillation (ref-009) and bias-aware distillation (ref-012).
